name: Open Banking Consent and Payment Initiation

phases.name: TPP Registration and Discovery
phases.description: A Third Party Provider (TPP) registered with the OBIE Directory (or Open Banking Ltd successor) discovers the bank's Open Banking API endpoints via the bank's developer portal and Well-Known endpoint. The TPP presents a valid OBIE-signed Software Statement Assertion (SSA) and completes Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) against the bank's authorisation server. The bank validates the TPP's FCA authorisation (PISP permission required for payment initiation), verifies the Software Statement, and creates an ENT-031 TPPRegistration record. This phase is a one-time setup per TPP software statement and does not involve the customer.
actors: SVC-017 (Digital Channels — Open Banking API surface)
entry_conditions: TPP holds a valid FCA PISP authorisation (or equivalent EEA passport recognised under UK transitional period)
TPP holds a valid OBIE-issued Software Statement
Bank's Open Banking Well-Known endpoint is available (GOV-006-R01: 99.5% uptime obligation)
exit_conditions: TPP has received a client_id and client_secret via DCR response
ENT-031 TPPRegistration record created with status = active
TPP's redirect_uris registered and validated

phases.name: Consent Request
phases.description: The TPP constructs a Domestic Payment Consent resource using the OBIE v3.1.x Domestic Payment Consents API (POST /domestic-payment-consents). SVC-017 (channel) validates the request against the OBIE schema, checks the TPP's client credentials, and creates an ENT-030 OpenBankingConsent record with status = awaiting_auth. SVC-017 returns a consent_id and a redirect URL. The TPP redirects the customer's browser to the bank's authorisation endpoint with the consent_id embedded in the authorisation request. The customer arrives at the bank's authentication journey.
entry_conditions: PH-035 complete — TPP holds a valid client_id
TPP has a customer who has initiated a payment flow on the TPP's own application
Payment details (amount, payee sort code, payee account number, payee name, reference) are known to the TPP
exit_conditions: ENT-030 OpenBankingConsent created with status = awaiting_auth
Customer browser redirected to bank's authorisation endpoint with consent_id and state parameter
consent_id returned to TPP in Domestic Payment Consents response

phases.name: Customer Authentication and Consent Confirmation
phases.description: The customer authenticates with the bank using Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) via SVC-100. SCA must meet PSD2 RTS requirements: possession factor (registered mobile device) plus inherence factor (biometric) or knowledge factor (PIN), with dynamic linking binding the SCA to the specific payment amount and payee. After successful SCA, the bank displays the payment details (amount, payee, reference) for the customer to confirm. On confirmation, SVC-017 calls SVC-100 to issue an authorisation code. ENT-030.status transitions to authorised and ENT-030.sca_completed is set to true. EVT-059 ConsentAuthorised is published. The customer's browser is redirected back to the TPP's redirect_uri with the authorisation code. If the customer declines, ENT-030.status = revoked and EVT-060 ConsentRevoked is published.
entry_conditions: PH-036 complete — ENT-030 exists with status = awaiting_auth
Customer has been redirected to the bank's authorisation endpoint
Payment details are displayed to the customer for consent (Consumer Duty — Understanding outcome)
exit_conditions: Happy path: ENT-030.status = authorised, ENT-030.sca_completed = true, EVT-059 published
Customer declines: ENT-030.status = revoked, EVT-060 published, redirect to TPP with error
SCA timeout/failure: ENT-030.status = expired, redirect to TPP with error

phases.name: Payment Initiation
phases.description: The TPP exchanges the authorisation code for an access token at SVC-100's token endpoint, then calls POST /domestic-payments on SVC-017 (channel) with the consent_id and the original payment details. SVC-017 validates that the consent_id is authorised, not consumed, and not expired. SVC-017 then makes a synchronous REST call to SVC-001 (Retail Banking Core, CAP-001) to create a PaymentIntent (ENT-008) — this is a channel-to-capability call, explicitly permitted by the architectural principle that channels may call capability REST APIs synchronously. SVC-001 validates account status, available balance, and daily payment limit. On success, SVC-001 creates ENT-008 and publishes EVT-179 (PaymentIntentCreated). SVC-017 updates ENT-030.status = consumed and sets the open_banking_payment_id cross-reference. EVT-061 OpenBankingPaymentInitiated is published by SVC-001. SVC-017 returns a payment_id and status = AcceptedSettlementInProcess to the TPP.
entry_conditions: TPP holds a valid access token bound to the consent_id
Payment details in the POST /domestic-payments request match those in the stored consent
exit_conditions: ENT-008 PaymentIntent created with status = pending_screening
ENT-030.status = consumed
EVT-179 PaymentIntentCreated published by SVC-001
EVT-061 OpenBankingPaymentInitiated published by SVC-001
TPP receives HTTP 201 with payment_id and status = AcceptedSettlementInProcess

phases.name: Payment Execution
phases.description: The JRN-002 event-driven payment execution flow is reused in full. EVT-179 (PaymentIntentCreated) is consumed concurrently by SVC-051 (Sanctions Screening) and SVC-013 (Fraud Detection). SVC-051 publishes EVT-180 (SanctionsScreeningCompleted); SVC-013 publishes EVT-181 (FraudScoreCompleted). SVC-001 correlates both results on payment_intent_id: if both clear, it publishes EVT-182 (PaymentCleared); if sanctions hit, it publishes EVT-185 (PaymentFailed) with reason sanctions_review; if fraud block, it publishes EVT-186 (PaymentFraudBlocked). On PaymentCleared, SVC-009 (Domestic Payments, CAP-003) consumes the event, constructs an ISO 20022 pacs.008 message, and submits to Vocalink FPS. SVC-009 creates ENT-009 (PaymentExecution) and publishes EVT-183 (PaymentExecuted). SVC-001 consumes EVT-183, debits the account ledger, updates PaymentIntent.status = completed, and publishes EVT-184 (AccountDebited) and EVT-062 (OpenBankingPaymentCompleted). On any failure path, SVC-001 publishes EVT-063 (OpenBankingPaymentFailed).
entry_conditions: PH-038 complete — EVT-179 published and available on topic payments.initiation
exit_conditions: Happy path: PaymentIntent.status = completed, EVT-184 published, EVT-062 published
Sanctions failure: PaymentIntent.status = sanctions_blocked, EVT-185 published, EVT-063 published
Fraud failure: PaymentIntent.status = fraud_blocked, EVT-186 published, EVT-063 published
FPS rejection: PaymentIntent.status = failed (failure_reason = fps_rejection), EVT-185 published, EVT-063 published

phases.name: Status Polling and Confirmation
phases.description: The TPP polls GET /domestic-payments/{DomesticPaymentId} on SVC-017 (channel) to retrieve the current payment status. SVC-017 maps the internal PaymentIntent.status to the OBIE payment status enum (AcceptedSettlementInProcess | AcceptedSettlementCompleted | Rejected). On completion, SVC-053 (Notification Service) dispatches a push notification or in-app message to PER-001 confirming payment success. On failure, the customer is notified with the failure reason (suitably redacted — fraud block reasons must not be disclosed to the customer). The TPP may also subscribe to the bank's event notification webhook if supported (OBIE Event Notification API).
entry_conditions: PH-038 complete — TPP holds a payment_id
payment_id maps to an ENT-008 record in SVC-001
exit_conditions: TPP has received final status (AcceptedSettlementCompleted or Rejected)
PER-001 has received a push notification confirming payment outcome
ENT-030.status = consumed (terminal — no further poll allowed)

happy_path.description: TPP completes DCR → posts consent → customer authenticates via SCA and confirms → TPP initiates payment → sanctions and fraud checks both clear → FPS executes → account debited → TPP polls and receives AcceptedSettlementCompleted → customer notified.

alternative_paths.name: Customer Declines Consent
alternative_paths.description: At PH-037, the customer reviews the payment details and declines. ENT-030.status = revoked. EVT-060 ConsentRevoked is published. The customer's browser is redirected back to the TPP with an access_denied error. The TPP surfaces an appropriate error to the customer. No payment is initiated.

alternative_paths.name: Consent Expires Before Initiation
alternative_paths.description: The customer authorises the consent (PH-037) but the TPP does not call POST /domestic-payments within the consent expiry window (max 90 minutes from authorisation per OBIE standards). SVC-017 rejects the payment initiation request with a 400 Consent Expired error. ENT-030.status = expired. The TPP must restart the consent flow from PH-036.

alternative_paths.name: Insufficient Funds at Initiation
alternative_paths.description: At PH-038, SVC-001 validates the account balance on receipt of the synchronous POST from SVC-017. If the available balance is less than the payment amount, SVC-001 returns an error to SVC-017, which returns HTTP 422 to the TPP with ErrorCode = UK.OBIE.Rules.AccountNotFound or a payment-specific error. ENT-008 is not created. ENT-030.status remains authorised (the consent was valid; the execution was refused). The TPP must inform the customer.

exception_paths.name: Sanctions Hit
exception_paths.description: During PH-039, SVC-051 returns a sanctions hit on EVT-179. SVC-001 publishes EVT-185 (PaymentFailed, reason = sanctions_review). SVC-001 also publishes EVT-063 (OpenBankingPaymentFailed). MLRO is alerted. PaymentIntent.status = sanctions_blocked. The TPP polls and receives status = Rejected. The customer receives a generic 'payment could not be processed' notification — the sanctions hit reason is not disclosed (tipping-off prohibition, POCA 2002 s333A).

exception_paths.name: Fraud Block
exception_paths.description: During PH-039, SVC-013 returns risk_level = block on EVT-179. SVC-001 publishes EVT-186 (PaymentFraudBlocked) and EVT-063 (OpenBankingPaymentFailed). PaymentIntent.status = fraud_blocked. The TPP polls and receives status = Rejected. The customer receives a generic notification that the payment could not proceed — the fraud block reason is not surfaced to prevent fraud evasion. Fraud case management follows the JRN-005 pattern.

exception_paths.name: FPS Submission Timeout
exception_paths.description: During PH-039, SVC-009 submits to Vocalink FPS but does not receive a response within the FPS scheme timeout (20 seconds). SVC-009 transitions PaymentExecution.status = timeout_pending_retry, retries once. On second timeout, SVC-009 publishes a failure event. SVC-001 transitions PaymentIntent.status = failed (failure_reason = fps_timeout) and publishes EVT-063. The TPP receives Rejected status.

design_decisions.decision: SVC-017 (Digital Channels) is treated as a channel service outside the system boundary, not as a capability. The Open Banking API surface is owned by SVC-017 but all business logic — consent persistence (ENT-030), payment intent creation (ENT-008), payment execution — lives in the capabilities it calls.
design_decisions.rationale: The architectural principle distinguishes channels (outside the system boundary, may call capability REST APIs synchronously) from capabilities (inside the boundary, cross-capability communication via async events only). SVC-017 is explicitly a channel service for CAP-007. Treating it as a capability would incorrectly place consent management and payment intent ownership in the channel layer, violating the separation of concerns. ENT-030 is owned by SVC-001 (CAP-001) because consent is a customer-account concern and must persist in the core banking aggregate.
alternatives_considered: Make SVC-017 a capability service owning ENT-030 (OpenBankingConsent)
Create a separate Open Banking capability service to own ENT-030 and ENT-031
design_decisions.rejected_because: Placing ENT-030 in SVC-017 (a channel) would mean consent records — which are authoritative customer account objects governed by PSR 2017 — live in a layer that may be replaced or replatformed independently of core banking. This creates regulatory risk. A separate capability service for Open Banking consent was considered but rejected because consent is inherently a customer-account relationship (customer_id, account_id, consent_type) that belongs in the retail banking core entity model.

design_decisions.decision: The SVC-017 → SVC-001 call for payment intent creation is a synchronous REST call (channel → capability). This is the single permitted cross-boundary synchronous call in this journey.
design_decisions.rationale: The channel must return a payment_id synchronously to the TPP in the POST /domestic-payments response (OBIE API contract requirement). The TPP uses this payment_id for subsequent status polling. An asynchronous pattern would require the channel to hold state and introduce a polling or callback mechanism within the channel layer, which is unnecessary complexity. The architectural principle explicitly permits channels to call capability REST APIs synchronously.
alternatives_considered: Asynchronous payment intent creation with a webhook callback from SVC-001 to SVC-017
design_decisions.rejected_because: OBIE POST /domestic-payments must return a payment resource with a DomesticPaymentId in the HTTP 201 response. Async creation would require SVC-017 to hold a pending payment_id and either block waiting for SVC-001 or implement a complex async-to-sync bridge within the channel layer. The synchronous channel → capability call is cleaner and consistent with the architectural principle.

design_decisions.decision: PH-039 fully reuses the JRN-002 event-driven payment execution chain (EVT-179 through EVT-186). No new payment events are introduced for the execution phase itself.
design_decisions.rationale: The Open Banking payment is a Faster Payment — it uses the same FPS rail, the same sanctions screening (SVC-051), the same fraud detection (SVC-013), and the same domestic payment execution (SVC-009). Introducing separate events for the OB payment execution would duplicate the payment event topology without adding value. The open-banking-specific events (EVT-061, EVT-062, EVT-063) serve as wrapper signals for the TPP notification layer and status mapping, while the core payment events remain shared.
alternatives_considered: Create a parallel OB-specific payment event chain (OBPaymentIntentCreated, OBSanctionsCompleted, etc.)
design_decisions.rejected_because: A parallel event chain would duplicate the screening, fraud, and execution topics and require SVC-051, SVC-013, and SVC-009 to have OB-specific handlers. This violates DRY, complicates event routing, and creates a maintenance burden. The distinction between a standard payment and an OB-initiated payment is captured at initiation (EVT-061) and completion (EVT-062/EVT-063) only.

design_decisions.decision: ENT-030 (OpenBankingConsent) is owned by SVC-001 (Retail Banking Core), not by SVC-017 (Digital Channels).
design_decisions.rationale: Consent is a legally significant customer-account agreement under PSR 2017. It binds a specific customer (customer_id) to a specific account (account_id) for a specific payment to a specific payee. This is a core banking record, not a channel-layer session artefact. SVC-001 already owns Customer (ENT-001) and Account (ENT-004) — consent naturally extends this aggregate. Placing consent in SVC-001 enables SVC-001 to enforce the consent state machine (awaiting_auth → authorised → consumed) atomically with payment intent creation.
alternatives_considered: Own ENT-030 in SVC-017 (Digital Channels channel service)
design_decisions.rejected_because: SVC-017 is a channel service — it does not maintain persistent domain state. Moving ENT-030 to SVC-017 would create a domain entity with PSR-regulated lifecycle in a layer that has no persistent state ownership.
